status_summary: No FAA or DOT rulemaking to reform slot allocation was found; Federal Register searches for slot actions since 2025-01-20 returned orders, extensions, notices and an exemption only. The FAA issued scheduling-limit orders at Newark in 2025 (published 2025-05-23 and 2025-06-10) and at Chicago O'Hare (published 2026-04-20), and on 2026-06-23 published unchanged extensions of the LaGuardia and JFK orders to 2028-10-28, the JFK notice saying the FAA will continue to consider potential rulemaking to codify slot-control policies. On 2026-10-08 the FAA granted an exemption letting Spirit transfer 22 LaGuardia slots to JetBlue with conditions. These are capacity, extension and exemption actions, not a slot allocation rulemaking.

timeline.event: FAA published an order setting temporary hourly scheduling caps at Newark through 2025-12-31, built on voluntary schedule reductions and not a new allocation system.

FAA published a temporary daily scheduling cap order for Chicago O'Hare effective 2026-05-17 to 2026-10-24, allocated by share of Summer 2025 schedules and citing capacity, safety and preserving the competitive status quo.
FAA published an extension of the LaGuardia slot order to 2028-10-28 stating no changes to its allocation provisions.

FAA published an extension of the order limiting operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport to 2028-10-28, effective 2026-10-25, with no substantive changes; the notice says the FAA will continue to consider potential rulemaking to codify policies for slot-controlled airports.

FAA published a grant of a JetBlue and Spirit petition for exemption at LaGuardia permitting Spirit to transfer 22 slots to JetBlue, with no trade or lease until after April 2028 and a use-or-lose waiver through April 2027; it is a single-transaction exemption, not an allocation rulemaking.
